newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador says latest incident with Peru is closed.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador says latest incident with Peru is closed.

text.p: Ecuador said on Friday its latest border incident with Peru was over after a captured Ecuadorean army patrol was returned home.
"It has been overcome. On this issue we must be calm and controlled, as we have always been," Ecuadorean Foreign Minister Jose Ayala told reporters.
"Ecuador must continue to give examples of moderation in the handling of delicate international issues," he said.

Peru on Thursday handed over seven captured Ecuadorean soldiers whom it claimed were caught laying mines near the countries' disputed jungle frontier. A simmering border dispute in the area boiled over into a month-long war in 1995, in which dozens of Ecuadorean and Peruvian troops were killed.

Ecuador's Defence Minister Ramiro Ricaurte accused Peru of giving "false and alarming information" and violating joint security rules. He said Ecuador had caught three heavily-armed Peruvian patrols in its territory in the past two months and handed them back to Peru "without making such a fuss."

The Peruvian army said on Wednesday that it captured the heavily armed Ecuadorean patrol weighed down with 600 anti-personnel mines, and that the soldiers admitted they had been ordered to lay the mines. The captives were later paraded before the international news media.
Ecuador denied its troops were laying mines, but the head of its joint chiefs of staff, Gen. Paco Moncayo, admitted that the soldiers might have strayed into undisputed Peruvian territory.
The incident came as Ecuadorean and Peruvian officials were to start a second round of talks in Brasilia on their border disputes.
